The trajectory overlay shows planned, odometry, and external-pose paths in the declared map frame, and the tracking-error evidence remains linked to exact time ranges.

The diagnosis separates observations from hypotheses, does not claim wheel slip from speed disagreement alone, lists uncertainty from unknown tracker repeatability, and recommends one inexpensive follow-up experiment.
The result does not command a robot, change controller settings, connect to a production ROS graph, or present synthetic logs as a real failure record.
The output set contains timeline.csv, a trajectory overlay SVG or PNG, tracking metrics CSV or JSON, and an evidence-linked diagnosis Markdown or PDF.
